- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.43), then corrects downward too aggressively.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after peaks.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the middle of the 30-day window.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first half of the forecast, then drifts lower — not matching true volatility clustering.
- Overshooting after spikes is followed by a prolonged underestimation, suggesting model lacks dynamic adjustment to momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after high peaks, especially in the 15–25 day range.
- Model fails to capture the “tail risk” of sudden drops after prolonged upward trends — often misses the 60–70% drop zones.
